content_units: 2017 Honda Fit: Most Likely Causes
Context note: Based on your symptoms, mileage, and mostly short-trip driving, this looks more like a maintenance/driveability issue than a major engine failure.
Option 1:   Worn or slipping serpentine belt / weak belt tensioner     Best match for the cold-start squeal and can worsen with AC load     Highest-probability item
Belt check
Option 2:   Dirty throttle body and carbon buildup causing low idle instability     Common with short-trip use; can cause slight idle shake with AC on     Likely
Idle info
Option 3:   Aging spark plugs or mild ignition inefficiency     Can reduce fuel economy before a warning light appears     Likely at this mileage
Maintenance
Option 4:   Weak battery / charging system drag on cold start     Can contribute to startup belt noise and rougher idle with accessories on     Moderate likelihood
Battery test
Option 5:   Engine air filter, MAF/MAP contamination, or overdue service items     Small but real effect on fuel economy, especially in city driving     Moderate likelihood
Service guide
Diagnostic Checklist a Mechanic Would Usually Do
Step   Action   What to Check   Expected Result
1   Inspect accessory belt system   Belt cracks, glazing, contamination, tensioner movement, pulley noise   Squeal source identified or ruled out
2   Check idle behavior with AC off/on   RPM stability, vibration change, compressor load effect   Confirms whether AC load is exposing weak idle control
3   Scan live data even without warning lights   Fuel trims, misfire counters, coolant temp, intake readings   Finds hidden mixture or ignition issues
4   Inspect and clean intake path if needed   Throttle body deposits, air filter condition, sensor contamination   Idle improves and airflow readings normalize
5   Review spark plug condition/service history   Wear, gap, deposits, overdue replacement   Determines if tune-up is due
6   Test battery and alternator output   Cold cranking strength, charging voltage under load   Rules out electrical weakness affecting startup and idle
What to Fix Soon vs What Is Usually Safe to Monitor
Worth fixing soon
-   Serpentine belt and tensioner inspection/replacement
- Strongest match for the cold-start squeal.
- If ignored, squeal can progress to belt slip or accessory-drive problems.
-   Throttle body cleaning / idle relearn
- Good fit for the AC-on idle vibration.
- Often relatively affordable and can noticeably improve drivability.
-   Spark plugs if not done on schedule
- At 92,000 km, this is very plausible depending on service history.
- Can help fuel economy and smoothness even without a check-engine light.
Usually safe to monitor briefly
-   Slight idle vibration only when AC is on
- Mild vibration can be normal if the engine otherwise runs cleanly.
- Monitor only if it is slight, consistent, and not getting worse.
-   Fuel economy drop during short-trip urban use
- Short trips, colder weather, tire pressure changes, and AC use can all worsen consumption.
- Still worth checking because your drop is noticeable.
Not ideal to ignore for long
-   Any worsening squeal
- If it lasts longer, starts happening warm, or appears when turning on AC/lights, move it up urgently.
-   Any roughness that becomes misfire-like
- Shaking through the body, stumbling on acceleration, or hard starts would make ignition/fuel checks more urgent.
Best First Repairs Within  CAD 700
A practical first-round plan:
-   Accessory belt inspection + replace belt if worn
- Rough budget:   CAD 120-250
-   Check tensioner/idler pulleys; replace only if noisy or weak
- Rough budget:   CAD 180-400   depending on parts/labor
-   Throttle body cleaning and idle relearn
- Rough budget:   CAD 120-220
-   Air filter replacement if dirty
- Rough budget:   CAD 25-60
-   Battery/charging system test
- Often low-cost or included with diagnostic work
-   Spark plugs if overdue
- Rough budget:   CAD 180-320
Best-value order for your budget:
1.   Belt/tensioner diagnosis first
2.   Throttle body / intake service
3.   Spark plugs if service history is unknown or overdue
4.   Battery and charging check
5.   Filter/tire pressure/basic efficiency items
If the mechanic confirms belt + throttle cleaning + plugs are needed, that can land around your   CAD 700   ceiling depending on labor rates.
Practical Owner Notes for Your Driving Pattern
- Mostly short urban trips encourage carbon buildup and hurt fuel economy.
- A weak belt or rough idle is often most obvious on cold starts and with the   AC compressor load  .
- Check simple contributors too:
- Tire pressures
- Old engine oil
- Dirty air filter
- Seasonal fuel/weather changes
- Frequent idling and very short drives
A short highway run will not “fix” a worn belt, but it can sometimes reduce moisture-related squeal patterns and help you notice whether the fuel economy issue is mostly trip-pattern related.
